title: Midnight ops bridging notes — synthesis & follow-ups
body:
SUMMARY:
- Short: transient p99/p999 latency spikes observed across inference-proxy behind the autoscaler between 00:30-01:15 PST. Partial mitigation applied; system stable now but follow-ups required.
- Environment: production-us-west1 cluster (k8s prod-1), services primarily impacted: inference-proxy (frontend), kv-cache (redis cluster), routing-service.

KEY EVENTS TIMELINE (local times):
- 00:29: first weak uptick in tail latency (p99 ~ 900ms).
- 00:31: spike to p99 ~1.8s and p999 ~7.2s; error budget alert (pager) triggered for inference-proxy route /v1/generate.
- 00:33: automated autoscaler attempted scale-up but new pods failed readiness check (startup time exceeded).
- 00:40: manual rollback of last infra config (kube rolling config change from 00:05) initiated; new pods still slow.
- 00:45: found KV cache miss storm—redis nodes reporting high blocked clients and CPU bursts.
- 00:52: evicted several stale client connections; temporarily raised redis maxclients and applied CONFIG SET timeout to prune hung clients.
- 01:05: gradual recovery: p99 dropped back under 600ms, p999 under 2s.
- 01:12: incident declared resolved-to-monitor after 30 mins of stable metrics.

ACTIONS TAKEN (what I did):
- triaged alert in PagerDuty -> joined channel #sre-prod -> grabbed bridge.
- checked metrics (Datadog): inference-proxy latency, queue depth, pod restarts.
- kubectl describe + logs on problematic inference-proxy pods; saw blocked downstream connections to redis.
- Restarted one redis pod (redis-kv-3) to clear blocked clients; used kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis-kv --namespace=prod (see note).
- Temporarily increased redis maxclients from 10000 -> 14000 and set client-output-buffer-limit to protect against bursts.
- Rolled back the 00:05 kube scheduling change (nodeAffinity tweak) which coincided with pod placement on hot hosts.
- Left short run of synthetic traffic to validate recovery.

ESCALATIONS / COMMUNICATIONS: 
- Notified on-call infra lead (Tom N.) at 00:38 who approved immediate rollback.
- Notified product contact (Lana) at 00:50 for customer-facing possibility; asked CS to standby for any reports.
- Opened INC-2026-7 for postmortem tracking (linked above).

OPEN FOLLOW-UPS (actionable items for morning shift):
- A1: Deep-dive on redis blocked client root cause and tuning. Assign to eng-sre + infra (owner: Luca). Ticket INF-4382 created.
- A2: Add a targeted readiness probe / startup timeout guidance to inference-proxy runbook: current startup threshold (20s) is too aggressive when KV warmups happen. (owner: Aisha)
- A3: Revisit autoscaler cooldown and scale-up thresholds to prevent thrashing when redis temporarily slows. (owner: SRE-Platform)
- A4: Add automated alert that ties slow readiness failures + redis blocked clients as a composite signal. (owner: Observability)
- A5: Coordinate with platform to avoid scheduling affinity changes during high-traffic windows (proposal in INF-4382).
- A6: Run backfill tests on redis-client memory usage with synthetic prefix storms. (owner: Priya)

RUNBOOK NOTES / PROPOSED EDITS (draft content to insert):
- Section: "Redis blocked clients" -> Steps: 1) Check INFO command 'blocked_clients' and 'used_cpu_sys'. 2) If blocked_clients > 50 and CPU > 80% sustained -> consider rolling restart of one replica and incrementally increase maxclients by +20% with monitoring. 3) Commands to run: kubectl exec -it redis-kv-0 -- redis-cli INFO | egrep 'blocked_clients|used_memory_human|connected_clients' ; kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis-kv --namespace=prod; watch redis-cli -h <ip> INFO KEYSPACE.
- Add exact rollback commands and note the need to hold change approvals for 15 minutes after config changes.
- Add suggested probe tuning: readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds: 30 -> 45 for inference-proxy when kv-cache warming is expected.

OBSERVATIONS / CLUES:
- The timing aligns with a kube scheduling tweak at 00:05 that placed new inference-proxy pods onto nodes with other heavy workloads (batch jobs). Possibly noisy neighbor + redis pressure.
- Readiness fails looked like blocked IO waiting on redis socket timeouts, not app crash.
- Autoscaler logic scales by CPU by default; when redis is the bottleneck, CPU isn't enough signal. We need a custom HPA metric (queue length or inflight requests) rather than raw CPU.

NOTES TO SELF / TO-DOS IN DOC FORM:
- add links to the synthetic test harness used (TODO: store under /shared_drives/engineering/observability/synthetic-tests).
- capture exact redis config snapshot before changes (I have the copy at /tmp/redis-config-20260514.conf on my laptop).
- follow up with infra on why kube scheduling tweak was merged into prod without rollback window.

METRICS SNIPPET (quick numbers pulled during incident):
- inference-proxy p99: 1.8s peak -> steady 0.55s after fix.
- inference-proxy p999: 7.2s peak -> 1.9s after fix.
- redis blocked_clients: peaked at 230 -> back to <10 after restart.
- redis CPU: peaked at 96% on redis-kv-3.

MORNING HANDOFF (for next bridge / morning oncall):
- Current status: stable; monitoring watch for 4 hours.
- Primary follow-ups to pick: INF-4382 deep-dive (redis tuning + blocked client root cause), change to readinessProbe in inference-proxy runbook, review autoscaler metric strategy.
- If spikes recur: 1) escalate to infra lead and consider full redis rolling restart during low-traffic window, 2) enable circuit-breaker on routing-service to shed non-critical requests to protected paths.

QUESTIONS FOR MORNING (unresolved):
- Was there any concurrent maintenance on redis cluster (backup or compaction) at ~00:20? (ask infra/ops).
- Are we able to expose a queue-length metric from inference-proxy within the HPA pipeline quickly?
- Should we lock down scheduling-affinity merges during midnight maintenance windows?

ATTACHMENTS / LINKS (quick):
- INC-2026-7 (incident ticket): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-7
- INF-4382 (follow-up deep-dive): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4382
- Bridge chat summary: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01ABCDE12/p1634567890123456
- Runbook draft for redis: https://confluence.redwood.local/display/SRE/kv-cache-runbook

FINAL QUICK NOTES:
- No customer reports so far; CS team on standby.
- Recommend we postpone non-urgent infra-affinity changes until we have run replay tests.
- I logged the exact kubectl commands I ran in the incident channel for reproducibility.

-- Aisha (night shift)

[notes to morning: skim OPEN FOLLOW-UPS and RUNBOOK NOTES first before diving into INF-4382]
